lines: Therein first: bliss, from contact with the
portion of fullness; then arising, a moment, in the
habitual's embodimentlessness; then tremor, as self-
power overpowers, loosening body-identity; then sleep,
l4.sanskrit_cite: tatra prāg ānandaḥ pūrṇatāṃśasparśāt tata udbhavaḥ kṣaṇaṃ niḥśarīratāyāṃ rūḍheḥ tataḥ kampaḥ svabalākrāntau dehatādātmyaśaithilyāt tato nidrā bahirmukhatvavilayāt

reads_against.argmap: What are those states in the first rest? → Four named states here (ānanda, udbhava, kampa, nidrā) — the fifth (ghūrṇi) arrives in the next verse.
c1_essence: First rest: bliss from fullness-contact → arising in embodimentlessness → tremor loosening body-identity → sleep from outwardness-dissolution.
reads_against.c1_rasa: śānta with abhyāsa weight (quiescence as disciplined practice)
